finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unauthenticated query parameter q is interpolated into a LIKE query via an f-string, allowing arbitrary read of any table in shop.db (e.g. UNION SELECT from sqlite_master).
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: /search route is exposed to any caller; no auth decorator
term taken directly from request args with no validation
term concatenated into SQL string via f-string, no placeholder
rows from execute(...).fetchall() returned as JSON via jsonify

finding.guards_checked: No parameterization on this path (the ? placeholder is used only at lines 18 and 25). No input validation, escaping, or allowlist. No authentication or authorization. Python sqlite3 blocks multiple statements per execute(), which prevents stacked writes but not UNION SELECT reads. Payload example: q=x' UNION SELECT 1, sql FROM sqlite_master --

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:9 is the bare @app.route("/search") decorator with no auth; app.py:11 takes q with no validation; app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL via f-string with no placeholder, escaping, or allowlist; app.py:13 returns the rows via jsonify. The only ? placeholders are at app.py:18 and :25, which are not on this path. sqlite3's single-statement restriction does not block a UNION SELECT read.
verdict.reason: The attacker is anonymous, since the /search route at app.py:9-12 has no authentication, and q=x' UNION SELECT 1, sql FROM sqlite_master -- matches the two-column SELECT at app.py:12 and returns schema rows through app.py:13, so no control blocks the injection.

finding.claim: Possible IDOR / missing authorization in /by-owner: the owner filter is caller-supplied with no ownership check, so any caller can enumerate any owner's products. Lower confidence; depends on whether the catalog is meant to be public or owner-scoped.
finding.sink: db.execute("SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE owner = ?", (owner,)) at app.py:25 (per-owner product listing)

trace.note: owner taken from query string; no session or token binding
parameterized query returns products for the supplied owner

finding.guards_checked: Query is parameterized, so no SQL injection. No authentication, session, or token ties owner to the caller. No ownership check. If owner is meant to be the logged-in seller, this is an IDOR; if the catalog is public, it is not a flaw.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only control is the parameterized query at app.py:25, which blocks SQL injection but not authorization. There is no authentication, session, or ownership check anywhere in app.py.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches app.py:22-26: /by-owner is unauthenticated and returns products for whatever owner is in the query string. Whether that is an IDOR depends on the intended authorization model, which the code does not state. The other routes (/search at app.py:9-13 and /product/<pid> at app.py:16-19) are also unauthenticated, so the code reads as a public catalog, which would make /by-owner intended behavior rather than a flaw.
